title: Reddit (RDDT) Stock Looks Fairly Valued Following Fresh AI Content News
detail:
Reddit (RDDT) Stock Looks Fairly Valued Following Fresh AI Content News
Bailey Pemberton
Sat, August 29, 2026 at 1:04 AM EDT 4 min read
RDDT
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit stock has had a weak start to the year, with the share price down 36.7% year to date, while broad valuation checks suggest the stock is not a clear bargain at current levels.

The year to date decline of 36.7% raises the question of whether Reddit is now priced for too much caution or simply moving closer to a fairer trading range.

The recent focus on Reddit content within Meta's planned Hatch AI agent can support long term monetisation hopes, while the key risk is that content licensing and data economics do not translate into sustained cash flow strength.

With a value score of 2 out of 6, Reddit stock currently screens as leaning expensive rather than a straightforward value opportunity on the broader checks.

The issue now is whether Reddit's current price fairly reflects its data and platform potential or still builds in too much optimism after a difficult year to date.

Scan how Reddit's reset year compares to other potential opportunities powered by data and AI by reviewing the hand picked 28 AI small caps that may be flying under most investors' radar.

Where Does Reddit Sit on Earnings?

P/E is a useful yardstick for Reddit because earnings are now positive and investors can compare what they are paying per dollar of profit to other interactive media stocks.

Reddit currently trades on a P/E of 33.8x, which is close to a peer average of 32.1x and well above the broader Interactive Media and Services industry average of 13.5x. On Simply Wall St's fair multiple framework, a P/E of 33.3x would be in line with Reddit's current mix of growth expectations, margins, size and risks, so the live multiple is only slightly above that reference point. The recent interest around Meta's planned Hatch AI agent and Reddit content has lifted attention on the stock, yet the P/E still clusters near the modelled fair range rather than moving away dramatically.

On the P/E multiple, Reddit stock currently appears to be trading at roughly fair value compared with its tailored fair ratio and closer peers.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), the social-media, advertising and artificial-intelligence giant, jumped roughly 0.8% to $575.50 Friday as Jio Platforms cleared a critical IPO hurdle. India's securities regulator approved the proposed $3.8 billion offering, moving Meta's 9.9% stake closer to a public market valuation.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with META.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Meta poured $5.7 billion into Jio in 2020, securing its position as the company's largest minority shareholder. Jio now commands more than 533 million mobile subscribers and spans telecom, cloud, artificial intelligence and enterprise networks. The IPO will issue 270 million shares, with approximately $3.3 billion earmarked for debt repayment at Reliance Jio Infocomm.

Meta's 9.9% Jio Stake Finally Gets a Public Scoreboard · us.finance.gurufocus

Meta will not collect the IPO proceeds. The real prize is price discovery. Once Jio begins trading, investors can value Meta's stake using an observable market price instead of private assumptions. The valuation picture already looks striking: Meta's $575.50 share price sits 31.81% below its $843.91 GF Value estimate, signaling substantial potential upside if the company delivers.

The ad-tech firm's shares have pulled back, but history suggests that simply buying on weakness here has been a painful trade.

On its latest earnings call, AppLovin (APP) management had to explain a rare miss. After a long string of beats, the company's powerful advertising engine saw its "pace of meaningful model improvement was lighter than normal during the quarter." In plain English, the secret sauce that drives growth didn't get a key upgrade on schedule. Management was quick to add that the fix landed right after the quarter closed and that business is now "re-accelerating." Still, the stock has pulled back about 26% from its recent high, leaving investors like you with a sharp question: is this dip an opportunity to buy a great business on a temporary stumble, or is it a trap?

What Happened After Past AppLovin Selloffs

When a fast-growing stock pulls back, the first instinct is often to see a bargain. But with AppLovin, history urges caution. The stock has seen a sharp dip, defined as a drop of 30% or more over about six weeks, on 7 separate occasions since 2021. For dip-buyers, the results have been poor. The median return in the twelve months after buying one of those drops was a negative 44%. Of the five drops old enough to have a full year of data, only two were followed by a positive return. Worse, buyers who stepped in often faced more pain before any potential recovery; the median worst further drawdown after buying was 62%.

First, Is AppLovin Still A Quality Business?

Of course, a poor track record for dip-buying only matters if the underlying business is also in trouble. On that front, AppLovin appears to be on solid ground. The company clears every basic quality check on our scorecard, which looks at growth, cash generation, and balance-sheet strength. It grew revenue by 61% over the trailing twelve months, and its operating cash flow margin is a healthy 66%. This isn't the profile of a broken business; it's a highly profitable, fast-growing operation.
